messages:
rachel: PSA: if your laptop dies mid-call, don't try to revive it by microwaving the battery. learned that today. :grimacing: never again.

omar: oh no. story time. how did it end?

rachel: long story short: it smoked, i unplugged, and we finished the demo on my phone's hotspot. also filed a tiny insurance report.

ben: microwaving batteries is a hard no. also glad you're okay. hotspot + phone camera = hero setup.

toni: quick poll: what's your go-to last resort for urgent calls? react: :iphone: tether, :electric_plug: run to neighbor for ethernet, :package: fresh battery swap, :fire: improvised antenna (do not microwave)

evelyn: tether for me. also, shoutout to @omar who lent me a USB-C dongle last week 60d

omar: anytime. pro tip: keep a tiny emergency kit (dongle, short ethernet, charger) near your door so you can dash to a cafe or a friend's if needed.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Noted increased tethering events from residential cluster R2 at 2026-10-03T15:22:00Z. Brief ISP latency spike 15:21:5815:23:10 UTC. No further action required.

rachel: thanks ops-bot. i'll add the emergency kit checklist to #devex. maybe a small sticker: "do not microwave".

evelyn: also, if anyone wants a spare dongle, i have one gathering dust in my drawer. drop by if you're in SF.

ben: reminder: label borrowed stuff. nothing worse than hunting for a tiny dongle during a demo.

toni: agreed. and call etiquette tip: if you're the presenter and seeing jitter, announce "switching to hotspot" so attendees don't panic. saved many faces.

rachel: lesson learned. will never attempt battery rituals again. thank you team. :heart:
